newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PC makers aim for bigger market share.
newsitem.headline: Japan PC makers aim for bigger market share.

text.p: Japan's top personal computer makers announced plans on Monday to boost production to grab a larger share of the booming worldwide computer market.

Toshiba Corp and NEC Corp, who are already major sellers of computers around the world, said they aim to boost those sales, while Fujitsu Ltd and Sony Corp said they will make a big push to gain international market share.

The global PC market is expected to grow by 18 percent to 83 million units in the year to next March 31, Japan's fiscal year, while the Japan market should see year-on-year growth of 25 percent to nine million units, said Mami Indo, an analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd.
"Japan's PC makers are getting down to work now that their brand names have come to be widely recognised in the United States and Europe, especially Toshiba and NEC," she added.
Toshiba was the only Japanese company in the top five for worldwide computer sales in the first quarter of this calendar year, with under five percent of the market.
The leader, Compaq Computer Corp of the United States, had 11.1 percent of the market. International Business Machines Corp was second, followed by Dell Computer Corp.
NEC Corp's partly owned U.S. unit Packard Bell-NEC was fourth.
NEC announced earlier on Monday that it would invest an additional $285 million in Packard Bell-NEC, taking NEC's total investment in the U.S. firm to $1.04 billion.
Sony, which is famous for its audiovisual products but not for computers, said its overseas strategy would centre on making PCs which can be easily combined with its other gadgets.

"We plan to produce PCs for home use. Our aim is to make computers that can be easily connected to other electronic equipment, such as digital movies and still cameras. This would add value to the products," a Sony spokesman said.
The spokesman did not reveal any production targets.

Toshiba, the top seller of portable computers worldwide, said it would increase its total PC output to four million units in fiscal 1997/98, up nearly 50 percent from a year earlier, with the additional supply of motherboards coming from a new plant in the Philippines.
Slightly more than three million of the computers would be made at its U.S. and German plants for sale overseas, with the rest made in Japan mainly for the domestic market.
"It is more efficient to have plants close to each market, as it enables PC makers to know their market, as well as to cut costs," Indo said.
NEC, which dominates the Japanese PC market with a 40 percent share, said it would raise production at home by about 15 percent to more than four million units in 1997/98.
An NEC spokesman said the additional investment in Packard Bell-NEC would help the U.S. firm strengthen its business in office-use PCs.

"We saw that combining our businesses would allow us to cooperate in the supply of parts and exchange know-how, as NEC is a big player in the corporate market and PB is a leading player in the home-use market," an NEC spokesman said.
Fujitsu, which has about 25 percent of the Japanese PC market, said it plans to boost worldwide PC output by 35 percent surge to 3.8 million units in 1997/98.
"We have just entered the U.S. market and realise it is necessary to show off the unique characteristics of our products in order to stand out," a Fujitsu spokesman said without elaborating.
"We market only notebook computers there, and we are working on developing those by using our know-how to the fullest extent," he added.
The company owns one plant in the United States and two plants in Europe, the spokesman said.
